observations: Not a defect, recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it: an issue recorded in_progress that holds no admission slot and waits in no line is taken out of the workflow by admission's releaseUnslotted on the next pass, which arms its linger — so a 'running tree' fixture must be slotted (seedSlotted) or the relay will fire on it legitimately. A first probe of mine used an unslotted in_progress root and read its relay as a defect; the debug run showed 'admission: released a root that held no slot and waited for none' before it, and the corrected probe refuses as it must.

dispatch.Actor.Person() (Kind == "user") and record.PersonActor (prefix user: with a non-empty id) disagree on one shape only: an actor of kind user with an empty id, which answers an awaiting root but relays no parked decision. Dispatch's own events always carry a non-empty actor id (its answer handler takes the authenticated human), and intake rejects nothing here, so the shape is unreachable from a real event; no test pins it and none should.

The architect's standing decision that a person's reply is kept as one row per comment, with the rows, the start-task string and the catch-up payload growing with a long discussion on a tree that stays parked, was not re-raised as a defect: it is recorded in the implementer's openQuestions and in the pull request's risk line.
